title: Majestic Geometry
reviewNotes: Reconstructed six-piece position after ...Rg8 at 77 seconds. Four checked branches compare unique winning Rd4, bishop-retreat rook sacrifices, a back-rank fork, and the drawn immediate rook capture. Earlier rook checks remain source context.
transcript: White is about to get a new queen, and it doesn't seem like black has any way to defend the promotion square. But, actually black can start with rook to F1 check, trying to misplace the white king. Naturally, the king wants to stay close to the pawn, but after rook to G1 with another check, we have a pretty difficult choice to make. [music] If the king goes in front of the pawn, now after bishop to D6, there is no way to break the king free from this cage. But, if the king goes, for example, to F8, after rook to C1, there is no way to prevent the rook from landing on the last rank and stopping the promotion. If you get a queen, there is going [music] to be a skewer. And since a bishop against a rook is a draw, this game is going to end pacifically. So, after rook to G1 check, white has to try and step behind the pawn, but little does white know that this is exactly the setup that black wanted to achieve. Because after bishop to D5, if white tries to get the queen, now there is going to be another skewer with rook to H1, and this is going to be yet again that draw with rook against bishop. So, naturally, white has to cover with rook to H4, and now the check is blocked, and the queen is about to be reborn. So, is white simply out of the woods? Well, not exactly. Black has the incredible and majestic rook to G8, a full rook sacrifice that, of course, cannot be accepted because this is still a draw. But, wait, not all is said and done. White can play rook to D4 and attack the bishop and the rook at the same time. Because, of course, the bishop has to stay on this diagonal to recapture the new queen. And if the bishop goes here, there is a fork, and the same thing goes for A2, there is going to be another fork. So, the bishop is left with only two choices, either B3 or E6. But, actually, if black plays bishop to B3, white has the stunning rook A4 check, a full rook sacrifice that cannot be accepted because remember the other rook is hanging and white gets a queen. And if black doesn't want to take the sacrifice, he will need to move the king to the b file [music] and now there is going to be another fork with the rook. So, this is not a possibility and the only available square to black is bishop to e6. But no, it isn't because of course white still has rook to d7, a brilliant similar sacrifice that of course if accepted is going to allow a promotion. And if the king moves for example here, there is going to be another fork. But wait a second, the king this time has one extra option of going to the last rank. But luckily we have placed this king exactly where we wanted him and white can finally take the rook and promote to a queen. Black cannot allow the queen to stay. Rook to d8 is going to fork these two pieces. And with a rook left, white is going [music] to win this game.
